channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Puka Nacua (MCL surgery) will be sidelined 4-5 months.
item.description: This confirms Nacua will not only miss the remainder of the regular season, but would be unavailable for any potential Super Bowl run for the pre-season favorites. Schefter did add that Nacua’s knee “checked out clean aside from the MCL.” That’s good news heading into Nacua’s potential free agency, though he is nevertheless at a low ebb in his up-and-down Rams tenure. The ups have been any time Nacua takes the field. The downs have been how often he has been sidelined, as well as his off-the-field issues. Going on 26, Nacua would make a lot of sense as a franchise tag candidate, or perhaps a tag-and-trade for the cap-leveraged Rams.-Patrick Daugherty

item.title: Panthers ruled out Jonathon Brooks (groin) for Week 11 against the Ravens.
item.description: Brooks will miss his seventh consecutive game in Week 11, leaving Chuba Hubbard to a true workhorse role for another week. The matchup is less than ideal against the Ravens but fantasy managers can continue riding the bump in volume to a high end RB2 profile for the veteran back.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Kyren Williams (toe) was limited Saturday but is expected to play in Week 12 against the Packers.
item.description: Williams is reportedly dealing with “soreness” in his toe and was limited in practice Saturday as a result. ESPN’s Sarah Barshop added that Williams is expected to play on Wednesday against the Packers. Expect him to continue working in a strict timeshare with Blake Corum coming out of the team’s Week 11 bye.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is doubtful for Week 11 against the Commanders.
item.description: Iosivas was practicing in full throughout the week, making his designation somewhat puzzling as he attempts to return from injured reserve. The team will have another week to activate the young wide receiver before he will be forced to remain on injured reserve for the remainder of the season.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Eagles placed WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) on injured reserve.
item.description: Wicks has already missed the previous three games with an ankle injury and now finds himself sent to injured reserve, meaning he will miss at least seven games total with poorly timed injuries. He saw a “foot” designation added to his status during a week of limited showings, which is presumably the issue that lands him on injured reserve. DeVonta Smith, who returns from an extended absence this week, Makai Lemon, and Darius Cooper are likely to hold down the starting wide receiver positions in Wicks’ absence.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Treylon Burks (foot) was removed from the injury report Saturday and will play in Week 11 against the Bengals.
item.description: Burks surprisingly went from a full session Thursday and a no-show Friday, prompting uncertainty regarding his expected availability for Monday Night Football against the Bengals. He quickly put those worries to rest with a full practice Saturday and was removed from the injury report. Expect Burks to continue operating in a featured role on the perimeter in the absence of Terry McLaurin.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Rachaad White (heel) is questionable for Week 11 against the Bengals.
item.description: White’s week of practice was troubling, first appearing on the injury report on Friday with a limited designation due to a heel ailment before being downgraded to a “DNP” Saturday. Even so, head coach Dan Quinn indicated the veteran back is “on track” for Monday Night Football. Assuming he is active, White is likely to slot back into the primary change of pace role behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt, the latter of whom appears set to be activated from injured reserve in time for Monday.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is questionable for Week 11 against the Bengals.
item.description: Croskey-Merritt managed a week of full practices as he attempts to return from injured reserve, and while the team has not yet activated him, he appears to be trending in the right direction for his first game action since Week 5. Rachaad White, also listed as questionable, would likely shift back to a primary change of pace role, should Croskey-Merritt return.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Steelers did not activate Michael Pittman (foot) ahead of Week 11.
item.description: Pittman will remain on injured reserve for at least another week. The team gets back fellow wide receiver Roman Wilson, who should join DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard as the starters from 11-personnel. Fantasy managers are likely only able to confidently start Metcalf against the Eagles.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Steelers activated WR Roman Wilson (hand) from injured reserve.
item.description: Wilson ended up staying on injured reserve for the minimum four games as he dealt with a hand injury, returning to a roster approaching full health, although fellow wide receiver Michael Pittman was not activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 11.Fantasy managers are likely only able to confidently start Metcalf against the Eagles on Sunday.-Mark Garcia
